9:["$","p","2",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"A USB-C hub or docking station solves this with a single cable. Plug one USB-C or Thunderbolt cable into your laptop and the dock handles the rest: video output, USB-A devices, ethernet, card readers, and laptop charging all through one connection."}}]
a:["$","p","3",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"The problem: the market is flooded with cheap hubs that throttle bandwidth, drop connections, and overheat. This guide cuts through the noise. We tested 14 hubs and docks across every price tier to find the ones worth your money in 2026."}}]
b:["$","h2","4",{"id":"hub-vs-docking-station-what-s-the-difference","children":"Hub vs. Docking Station: What's the Difference?"}]
c:["$","p","5",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Before buying, know what you actually need:"}}]
d:["$","p","6",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>USB-C Hubs</strong> are bus-powered, compact, and portable. They draw power from your laptop rather than the wall. Great for travel and occasional use at a coffee shop, but bandwidth is shared across all ports — run too many high-demand devices simultaneously and you'll see slowdowns."}}]
e:["$","p","7",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Docking Stations</strong> have their own power supply (usually 90W–180W AC adapter). They can charge your laptop at full speed, drive dual 4K monitors, and handle a full desktop replacement scenario. Heavier, designed to stay on your desk permanently."}}]
f:["$","p","8",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Thunderbolt Docks</strong> are docking stations that use the Thunderbolt protocol instead of generic USB-C. Thunderbolt 4 delivers 40 Gbps bandwidth — twice the 20 Gbps ceiling of USB 3.2 Gen 2. If you have a Thunderbolt laptop (most Intel-based Macs and many high-end Windows laptops), a Thunderbolt dock unlocks dramatically faster speeds and more reliable multi-monitor support."}}]
10:["$","p","9",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>The rule:</strong> USB-C hub for portability and budget. Thunderbolt dock for a permanent desk setup with a Mac or high-end Windows laptop. Standard USB-C dock for everything in between."}}]
11:["$","h2","10",{"id":"what-to-look-for","children":"What to Look For"}]
12:["$","h3","11",{"id":"bandwidth-and-protocol","children":"Bandwidth and Protocol"}]
13:["$","p","12",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"The single most important spec most buyers ignore. A hub labeled \"USB 3.2 Gen 2\" has a 10 Gbps ceiling — shared across <em>all</em> ports simultaneously. Plug in a fast SSD, a 4K monitor, and an ethernet connection at once and each gets a fraction of that bandwidth."}}]
14:["$","ul","13",{"children":[["$","li","0",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>USB 3.2 Gen 2</strong> — 10 Gbps total bandwidth. Fine for hubs with 1–2 USB-A ports and no video."}}],["$","li","1",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>USB 3.2 Gen 2×2</strong> — 20 Gbps. Enough for dual monitors + peripherals at moderate speeds."}}],["$","li","2",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Thunderbolt 4</strong> — 40 Gbps. The only spec that handles dual 4K monitors + fast storage + peripherals without throttling."}}]]}]
15:["$","h3","14",{"id":"power-delivery-pd","children":"Power Delivery (PD)"}]
16:["$","p","15",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Check two numbers: the dock's total wattage and the PD passthrough to your laptop. A 96W dock might only pass 60W to your laptop — fine for a MacBook Air, insufficient for a 16-inch MacBook Pro or a gaming laptop under load."}}]
17:["$","ul","16",{"children":[["$","li","0",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>MacBook Air / 13\" laptops</strong> — 60W PD minimum"}}],["$","li","1",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>MacBook Pro 14\"</strong> — 96W recommended"}}],["$","li","2",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>MacBook Pro 16\" / large Windows laptops</strong> — 100W minimum, 140W ideal"}}],["$","li","3",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Gaming laptops</strong> — 140W+ (many require their own charger regardless)"}}]]}]
18:["$","h3","17",{"id":"display-output","children":"Display Output"}]
19:["$","p","18",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Confirm your laptop's display protocol before buying. Apple Silicon Macs (M1 through M4) support DisplayPort Alt Mode but <em>not</em> Thunderbolt's video output over USB-C in the same way Intel Macs do — some docks behave differently across chip generations. AMD-based Windows laptops have their own quirks."}}]
1a:["$","ul","19",{"children":[["$","li","0",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Single monitor: nearly any dock handles this"}}],["$","li","1",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Dual 4K 60Hz: requires Thunderbolt 4 or a dock with a dedicated DisplayLink chip"}}],["$","li","2",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Triple monitor: requires DisplayLink — factor in the driver requirement on Mac"}}]]}]
1b:["$","h3","20",{"id":"build-quality-signals","children":"Build Quality Signals"}]
1c:["$","p","21",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Cheap hubs run hot because they use cut-rate controllers without adequate thermal management. Look for aluminum housings (better heat dissipation than plastic), braided cables, and controllers from reputable chipmakers: Realtek (ethernet), VIA Labs, Renesas, or Texas Instruments (USB controllers). Avoid hubs that don't list the chipset at all."}}]

64:["$","h2","93",{"id":"what-to-avoid","children":"What to Avoid"}]
65:["$","p","94",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Single-chip USB hubs under $20</strong> — these use a single hub controller for all ports. Every device shares the same bus. A USB webcam and an external drive will fight each other for bandwidth during video calls. Buy once, buy right."}}]
66:["$","p","95",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Hubs that list \"87W charging\" on a 100W adapter</strong> — the difference between the adapter rating and the passthrough rating represents heat, not power. A good dock should pass at least 85% of adapter power to the laptop. Anything lower means the hub is inefficient."}}]
67:["$","p","96",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>HDMI-only docks for Mac</strong> — Apple Silicon Macs have issues with HDMI over USB-C adapters that aren't properly implemented. Prefer DisplayPort or Thunderbolt video output when buying for a Mac with M-series chips. If a dock only offers HDMI and costs under $50, read the Amazon reviews specifically from Mac users before buying."}}]
68:["$","p","97",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Docks without a listed chipset</strong> — reputable manufacturers list their ethernet and USB controller chipsets (Realtek, VIA Labs, Renesas, TI). No chipset listed usually means a generic no-name controller prone to dropout and heat issues."}}]
69:["$","h2","98",{"id":"setting-up-your-dock-for-best-performance","children":"Setting Up Your Dock for Best Performance"}]
6a:["$","p","99",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Cable matters more than you think.</strong> A Thunderbolt 4 dock requires a certified Thunderbolt 4 cable. USB-C cables are not interchangeable — a cable that came with your phone charger won't deliver full bandwidth. Use the cable that came with the dock; if you need a longer run, buy a certified Thunderbolt 4 cable from Anker, CalDigit, or Cable Matters."}}]
6b:["$","p","100",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Ventilation.</strong> Place your dock where air can circulate around it. Never stack it under your laptop or sandwich it between books. The aluminum docks in this guide rely on passive cooling — airflow is their heatsink."}}]
6c:["$","p","101",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Driver hygiene on Windows.</strong> If you use a DisplayLink dock, keep the DisplayLink driver updated. Outdated drivers are the single biggest cause of connection drops and flickering monitors on Windows. Sign up for DisplayLink's update notifications."}}]
6d:["$","p","102",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Daisy-chaining Thunderbolt.</strong> If you use a Thunderbolt monitor, connect it to the dock's downstream Thunderbolt port, not directly to the laptop. This keeps the laptop's Thunderbolt port free for the dock and preserves full bandwidth to both the monitor and the dock's other ports simultaneously."}}]
6e:["$","h2","103",{"id":"frequently-asked-questions","children":"Frequently Asked Questions"}]
6f:["$","p","104",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Will a Thunderbolt dock work with a USB-C laptop?</strong>"}}]
70:["$","p","105",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Yes, with a caveat. A Thunderbolt 4 dock is backward compatible with USB-C, but it will only run at USB speeds (up to 10 Gbps), not Thunderbolt speeds (40 Gbps). Display output may also be limited — some Thunderbolt docks only output video over Thunderbolt, not USB-C Alt Mode. Check the dock's specs for USB-C compatibility before buying."}}]
71:["$","p","106",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Can I run dual monitors from a MacBook Air M3?</strong>"}}]
72:["$","p","107",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Yes, but only with external support. The M3 MacBook Air natively supports one external display. For dual monitors, you need a dock with DisplayLink (which adds a second display via software rendering) and the DisplayLink driver installed. The Plugable 14-in-1 handles this. Note: DisplayLink-connected monitors cannot play DRM content."}}]
73:["$","p","108",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Why does my dock get hot?</strong>"}}]
74:["$","p","109",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Some heat is normal. A dock charging your laptop at 85W and driving two monitors is moving significant power. Excessive heat (too hot to touch) usually means inadequate thermal design, a bad power supply, or a failing unit. If your dock is regularly burning hot, check ventilation first; if the problem persists, consider a return."}}]
75:["$","p","110",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Do I need a dock if I only use one monitor?</strong>"}}]
76:["$","p","111",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Not necessarily. A single USB-C to HDMI/DisplayPort adapter plus a separate USB-A hub and ethernet adapter can be cheaper. But if you're regularly connecting and disconnecting three or more devices, the single-cable convenience of a dock is worth the cost — especially if you use a laptop stand and want a clean desk."}}]
77:["$","p","112",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Is it worth spending more than $200 on a dock?</strong>"}}]
78:["$","p","113",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"For full-time desk workers: yes. The Thunderbolt docks in the $180–$280 range have dedicated power supplies, better thermal management, and more reliable firmware. The reliability difference between a $40 hub and a $200 dock is significant when your workflow depends on the connection staying stable across an eight-hour workday."}}]
